newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan toy maker Bandai says slow sales hit profits.
newsitem.headline: Japan toy maker Bandai says slow sales hit profits.

text.p: Japanese toy maker Bandai Co Ltd said on Tuesday that its profits in the half year to September fell more than 50 percent from the same period last year, due mainly to slower sales.
The company said it posted parent sales of 42.1 billion yen ($375 million) in the first half of the 1996/97 business year, down 22.5 percent from a year earlier.
Parent current profit fell even more sharply by 57.3 percent to 1.82 billion yen ($16.2 million).
Current profit is pretax profit and includes gains and losses made on securities investments and other non-operating activities.

"We made a mistake in reading market trends," said a Bandai spokesman. He said the best-selling toys were very inexpensive mini-cars priced at around 500 yen ($4), while Bandai's mainstay products, such as figures of television characters, were 10 times as expensive.
The company's earnings were also hit by sluggish sales of game software for 16-bit machines, the spokesman said.
The video game market has already switched to 32-bit machines, such as Sony Corp's PlayStation and Sega Enterprises Ltd's Saturn, which offer a better picture and more speed than the 16-bit machines.
To revive its game software business, Bandai plans to launch four game titles for 32-bit machines before the end of this year.
For the full year ending on March 31, the company expects to post 108 billion yen ($964 million) in sales and 10 billion yen ($89.2 million) in parent current profit. ($1=112 yen)
